newsitem.title: NORWAY: UK Fulmar oil to flow into Norpipe soon - Phillips.
newsitem.headline: UK Fulmar oil to flow into Norpipe soon - Phillips.

text.p: Crude from the Fulmar field in the British sector of the North Sea will begin to flow into the Norpipe system and join the Ekofisk oil stream by the end of the week, a spokesman from pipeline operator Phillips Petroleum said on Wednesday.
"Fulmar crude is due to start flowing into Norpipe on January 24 or 25," a Phillips spokesman said.
Fulmar collects about 125,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude from the Fulmar, Gannet, Clyde and Auk fields. Crude from the field is currently sent by shuttle tanker to the British mainland.
Fulmar is operated by Shell UK, a subsidary of the Royal/Dutch Shell Group.

The Fulmar blend will be mixed with Ekofisk output in the Norpipe via a Y-coupling. It will increase the Ekofisk stream landing at the Teesside terminal in northeast England to between 650,000 bpd and 700,000 bpd.

"Fulmar is a strategically vital area and the Norpipe connection may mean that several other UK fields choose to link up with the Teeside oil pipeline as time goes on," said Phillips' Ekofisk News newsletter.

Norpipe delivers Norway's Ekofisk area crude oil from six other Norwegian satellite fields to Teesside. The stream will be increased further when the company's 65,000 bpd British J-block fields come onstream in May.
